Theme

shy adjective

also bashful, timid, fearful of, fearful, easily frightened

classical

L&S
Plaut. Am. 3.2.22

verēcundus, verēcunda, verēcundum

declension

shy, bashful

Other words

  • timidus, timida, timidum — timid; fearful (of), with the genitive

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 314; Traupman 157

    Traupman 157 gives timidus, which is rather “fearful”.

  • meticulōsus (metuculōsus), meticulōsa, meticulōsum — full of fear, timid; not “meticulous”

    also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 293: Nūllust hōc metuculōsus aequē.; Plaut. Most. 1101: metuculōsa rēs (there “frightening”)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.; posteā Apul.)

    From metus. Ante- and post-classical (Lewis & Short). The English word has changed its meaning.

Examples

  • Nūllust hōc metuculōsus aequē.

    There’s no one so easily frightened as this fellow.Plaut. Amph. 293

See also be afraid.
